Pipeline Overview

What this repository builds

This repository runs a question-granular, citation-backed answering pipeline that turns a registry of research questions into a reviewed reference site, and it does so twice: once for a Spark Tuning Reference and once for the pipeline's own architecture[1]. Selection between the two happens via --corpus {spark,meta} on every pipeline script, defaulting to spark. scripts/corpus.py holds a Corpus dataclass with SPARK/META profiles, and every path a script touches (registry, per-question answers dir, section-projection dir, content-state sidecar, content manifest, references dir, Chroma path/collection, embedding model, build output, site title) comes from the selected profile rather than a hardcoded constant[1:1]. The spark corpus is the Spark Tuning Reference itself, built over references/ and indexed with the asymmetric question→passage retriever multi-qa-mpnet-base-dot-v1; its build output is index.html[1:2]. The meta corpus is this project's own architecture doc (docs/architecture.md, docs/runbook.md, docs/rules/*.md, AGENTS.md, and the agent/skill files that make up the pipeline). It is indexed via symlinks under references-meta/ with the general symmetric model all-mpnet-base-v2 into a separate Chroma collection, and its build output is meta.html[1:3]. The two corpora never share a registry, a Chroma collection, or a content manifest; each is an independent instance of the same pipeline shape[1:4].

Within either corpus, the atomic unit of the pipeline is the question, not the section: the registry (research/questions.yaml, or its meta counterpart) is the single source of truth holding sections and questions, and every other artifact is a derived projection, never edited directly as a source of truth[1:5]. Content flows one way through the pipeline: registry → per-question answer files (prose plus footnotes and their own ## Sources) → section projections (an ordered concatenation of a section's question answers, with sources merged and deduped) → content pages (brief-driven on first generation, human-owned after that) → the built site, and a downstream artifact is never treated as a source of truth for an upstream one[1:6]. The project's own AGENTS.md restates the operator-facing consequence: every content page is real cited prose, not a placeholder, and new or changed content still flows registry → answer → projection → page[2].

The build output is produced regardless of whether every content page is current. A committed hash sidecar tracks each content page against the sha256 of the section projection it was last generated or accepted from, classifying pages as ungenerated, stale, or ok; the build script checks this before rendering and prints a non-fatal warning banner listing any stale or ungenerated pages, but the build still produces index.html either way[1:7]. Recompute never triggers regeneration on its own; it only flags a page stale, since content pages are human-owned once generated[1:8].

On the Spark side, the resulting pages carry a further constraint tied to why the site exists: its manifest-level anchor IDs are a frozen cross-repo Integration Contract with the sibling sparkforensics repo, so renaming or removing one is a breaking change, and content assembly must read anchors from content/manifest.yaml rather than deriving them from a filename or heading[3]. That contract applies only to the Spark corpus; content/meta/manifest.yaml and meta.html carry no such contract, and their anchors may change freely[3:1]. docs/anchor-map.md reconciles the two, mapping each research answer file to its content file and frozen anchor[4].

The one-way derive chain

The chain runs in one direction, front to back:

research/questions.yaml → research/answers/q/<id>.md → research/answers/<section-id>.md → content/*.md (and content/bottlenecks/*.md) → index.html[1:9].

Each stage has a role. questions.yaml is the registry of sections and questions with their statuses. Each per-question answer file holds that question's prose plus its own [^id] footnotes and ## Sources block. The section file is a projection: an ordered concatenation of a section's question answers, with ## Sources merged and deduped, and it is the same path the content manifest's assembled_from: already points at. Content pages are brief-driven and only first-generated from that projection, after which they become human-owned. The build turns the content pages into index.html[1:10].

The architecture forbids treating any downstream artifact as a source of truth because research/questions.yaml is the single source of truth for the whole pipeline. Every other artifact (per-question answers, section projections, content pages) is a derived projection, regenerable from the registry and the per-question answer files, never edited as a source of truth itself[1:11]. The registry rules state this directly: never edit a downstream artifact as if it were the source of truth, since per-question answers, section projections, and content pages are all derived projections regenerable from the registry, and recompute always starts at questions.yaml and flows forward[5]. The derive-direction diagram states the same principle as an invariant: every arrow is one-way, and a downstream artifact (a section projection, a content page, the built site) is never a source of truth for an upstream one[1:12]. The project's own AGENTS.md restates the practical consequence for operators: new or changed content still flows registry → answer → projection → page, and questions.yaml remains the authoritative question registry rather than any prose plan or derived array[2:1].

Why the question, not the section, is the atomic unit

docs/architecture.md states the design directly: the atomic unit of the answering pipeline is the question, not the section. It goes on to name research/questions.yaml as the single source of truth, holding sections (id, num, title, default_k) as a grouping label and questions (id, section, text, version, k, status) as the working records. Every other artifact, from per-question answer files up through section projections and content pages, is a derived projection regenerable from the registry and those answer files, never a source of truth itself[1:13].

That per-question state (its own version, k, status) is what makes independent recompute possible. add_question.py mints an id and appends a single pending record without mutating any existing record, and recompute_question.py flips exactly one record back to pending and backs up only that question's old answer file, touching no other record or file[5:1]. If the section were the atomic unit, recomputing one question's answer would force treating the whole section's state as dirty; scoping status and versioning to the question lets one question be re-answered, re-versioned, or given its own k without disturbing its siblings.

The rest of the pipeline is built around that same grain: the Draft/Verify/Redraft agents are each scoped to a single question, and the answer-question skill runs one question end to end: Draft → Verify → [Redraft → re-Verify] → Humanize → check_prose → project_section → content_state ... → commit[1:14]. The meta corpus's own answer-meta-question skill mirrors this: its input is one question id, and it dispatches the Draft/Verify agents with a one-item question list equal to the record's text[6]. Only after a question is answered does project_section roll it into the section file, by concatenating that section's question answers in registry order and merging their ## Sources blocks[1:15]. The section projection is assembled from finished question-level work, not answered as a unit itself.
